trials.title: Tailwind v3 to v4 Migration Configuration Mismatch
trials.challenge: Migrating from Tailwind v3 (tailwind.config.js + @tailwind directives) to v4 (@import 'tailwindcss' + @plugin directives) with completely different configuration syntax and plugin loading
dead_ends: Tried using old @tailwind base/components/utilities directives - v4 doesn't recognize them
Attempted to keep tailwind.config.js alongside v4 - caused conflicts
Installed @tailwindcss/typography via npm before realizing v4 bundles it
Tried mixing v3 and v4 syntax in same project - resulted in compilation errors

breakthrough.what: Complete PostCSS configuration overhaul: replaced tailwindcss plugin with @tailwindcss/postcss, switched from @tailwind to @import 'tailwindcss', used @plugin directives for extensions
breakthrough.how: Updated postcss.config.js to use @tailwindcss/postcss, changed globals.css to use @import and @plugin syntax, removed tailwind.config.js entirely
breakthrough.why_it_works: Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first configuration where directives live in CSS files instead of JS config, PostCSS plugin handles new syntax

evidence_files.relevance: Complete v3 vs v4 syntax comparison table, migration patterns

before.state: Tailwind v3 config: tailwind.config.js required, @tailwind directives, require() for plugins, JS-based configuration
before.error: Build failures when attempting v4 syntax, plugin loading errors
before.blocking: Couldn't use v4 features, stuck with outdated patterns

after.state: Tailwind v4 CSS-first: no config file needed, @import 'tailwindcss', @plugin directives, CSS-based configuration
after.improvement: Clean build, access to v4 features, simpler configuration
after.metrics: Zero config file needed vs 100+ line v3 config, cleaner CSS imports

lessons_learned: Tailwind v4 philosophy: CSS-first configuration over JS config files
@import 'tailwindcss' replaces all three @tailwind directives (base/components/utilities)
Plugins bundled in v4 (typography, animate) - just use @plugin directive
PostCSS plugin changed from 'tailwindcss' to '@tailwindcss/postcss'
Migration requires updating PostCSS config, globals.css, removing tailwind.config.js
Simpler setup reduces configuration complexity

trials.title: Typography Plugin Prose Modifier Confusion
trials.challenge: Needed markdown styling with proper h1/h2/h3 sizing. Attempted prose element modifiers (prose-h1:text-5xl) without understanding they require base prose class and only override defaults, not replace them
dead_ends: Tried prose-h1:text-5xl without prose base class - no styling applied
Attempted to set --tw-prose-body CSS variables in :root - didn't affect content
Created 250-line manual component overrides for every HTML element - works but extremely verbose
Tried installing @tailwindcss/typography via npm first - unnecessary in v4

breakthrough.what: Typography plugin's prose class provides professional defaults in one line: <article className='prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert max-w-none'>
breakthrough.how: Added @plugin '@tailwindcss/typography' to globals.css, used prose class with size/dark mode variants
breakthrough.why_it_works: Typography plugin includes hand-tuned defaults for all HTML elements (headings, paragraphs, lists, code, tables), designed by professional designers for readability

evidence_files.relevance: Complete implementation log showing all 3 attempts (modifiers, overrides, plugin)
Typography plugin usage guide with size modifiers, element modifiers, dark mode
Final implementation using prose class for documentation rendering

before.state: 250-line manual component overrides for every HTML element (h1, h2, p, ul, ol, code, pre, blockquote, table, etc.)
before.error: Verbose, hard to maintain, easy to miss edge cases, custom styling for 15+ elements
before.blocking: Time-consuming to update, inconsistent styling across markdown content

after.state: One line: <article className='prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert max-w-none'>
after.improvement: Professional typography defaults, automatic dark mode, all HTML elements styled
after.metrics: 250 lines → 1 line (250x reduction), zero maintenance for typography updates

lessons_learned: Prose element modifiers (prose-h1:text-5xl) only work WITH base prose class
Element modifiers are for CUSTOMIZING defaults, not REPLACING them
Typography plugin provides professional hand-tuned defaults worth using
Manual component overrides give full control but at huge maintenance cost
prose, prose-lg, prose-xl size variants provide different base font sizes (16px, 18px, 20px)
dark:prose-invert automatically adapts all prose elements to dark mode
max-w-none removes default max-width (65ch) for full-width content
not-prose class sandboxes custom components within prose content

trials.title: Atomic Architecture Field Ordering Standardization
trials.challenge: 8 section components had inconsistent field ordering in Strapi admin: some started with content fields (items, roadmapItems), others with structural fields (background, badge, header). Created confusing UX where atomic components appeared in different positions across sections
dead_ends: Attempted to manually edit schema.json files without updating config sync - Strapi reverted changes
Tried reordering in Strapi UI Content-Type Builder - changes not persisted to files
Modified only frontend components without backend schemas - mismatched expectations

breakthrough.what: Standardized ALL section components to atomic architecture pattern: Background → Badge → Header → Component Content
breakthrough.how: Updated config sync JSON files (plugin_content_manager_configuration) with consistent field ordering, imported via Strapi config sync UI
breakthrough.why_it_works: Config sync as source of truth ensures field order persists across environments, consistent pattern improves developer UX and content editor experience

evidence_files.relevance: Complete refactoring summary showing before/after field ordering for 3 sections
Example config sync file showing background → badge → header → items ordering
Roadmap section with standardized field ordering

before.state: Inconsistent field ordering: FeatureGridSection (items first), RoadmapSection (roadmapItems first), FinalCTASection (ctaButtons first)
before.error: Confusing UX where atomic components (background, badge, header) appeared at different positions
before.blocking: Content editors had to hunt for structural fields, developers couldn't predict field order

after.state: All 8 sections follow atomic architecture: background → badge → header → content fields
after.improvement: Predictable field ordering, consistent admin UX, clear separation of structure vs content
after.metrics: 8/8 sections standardized (100%), 3 sections reordered (FeatureGridSection, RoadmapSection, FinalCTASection)

lessons_learned: Config sync JSON files are source of truth for field ordering in Strapi
Strapi UI changes don't persist to files without config sync export
Atomic architecture pattern: structural components before content
Consistent ordering improves both developer and content editor experience
Background → Badge → Header → Content is optimal visual hierarchy
Config sync import required after modifying config files
Clean build mandatory after schema changes to regenerate TypeScript types

critical_decisions.decision: Tailwind v4 CSS-First vs Keeping v3 JavaScript Config

options_considered.option: Keep Tailwind v3 with tailwind.config.js (status quo)
Hybrid approach: v4 PostCSS with v3 config file
Full migration to Tailwind v4 CSS-first configuration

critical_decisions.choice_made: Full migration to Tailwind v4 CSS-first configuration
critical_decisions.rationale: Tailwind v4 philosophy (CSS-first) aligns better with modern web development. Simpler configuration reduces complexity. Performance improvements and future features worth migration cost. Team benefits from learning current best practices.

trade_offs.gained: Cleaner configuration (no JS config file), CSS-based plugin loading (@plugin directive), faster builds (optimized PostCSS), access to v4 features
trade_offs.sacrificed: Familiarity with v3 patterns (acceptable - team learns), some documentation clarity (v4 docs evolving, but official guides available)
trade_offs.acceptable_because: Long-term maintainability more important than short-term familiarity, simpler config reduces future debugging, v4 is the future

critical_decisions.validation: Successful migration completed, builds working, no performance regression, team adapted to new syntax quickly
critical_decisions.long_term_implications: Project positioned for future Tailwind updates, simpler config reduces onboarding time for new developers, CSS-first approach more intuitive for CSS-focused developers
